sentences.text: The brief facts of the plaint are that the predecessor in interest of plaintiffs namely Sh. Tikam Singh and Sh. Sant Singh were the owners of about 250 Bighas of land situated within the Revenue Estate of Village Gharoli.

It is stated that out of the said land they made construction on the land measuring 10 bighas, 16 biswa comprising in Khasra No. 312, 780, 877, 888 and built some area in another land for GHER purpose.

It is further stated that notification no. F-8(67).76, L&B dated 17.11.1980 under Section 4 of Land Acquisition Act was issued for acquisition of land of village Gharoli, measuring 2600 bighas 12 biswa however, later on the land measuring 296 bigha 17 biswa was left out from acquisition as the said area was found to be densely populated and built up.

It is further stated that a part of the said construction made by the plaintiffs was demolished by the DDA and police and therefore the father of the plaintiff Sh. Tikam Singh filed a suit for recovery of compensation and declaration and permanent injunction which was decreed vide judgment dated 22.05.2013 by the Ld. ADJ.
It has been stated that father of plaintiff Sh. Tikam Singh has also raised some construction for the purpose of maintaining GHER for cattle food, Khor and Khontas in Khasra no. 318.

It is further stated that the said Khasra was acquired by the Government, however, a part of the said land which was in possession of the predecessors of the plaintiff was left out at the time of acquisition.

It has been stated that a part of the land of Khasra no. 318 has remained in actual Civ Suit 6703/16 Surat Singh VS. DDA 2/19 physical possession and enjoyment of Sh.
Tikam Singh and thereafter, in possession of his sons i.e. plaintiffs and their brothers.

sentences.text: 21. Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the plaintiffs has averred that the plaintiffs are the rightful owners of the suit land on the basis of the documents which have been exhibited by the plaintiffs.
It has also been stated that the suit land has never been acquired by the DDA.
Therefore, DDA has no right over the suit land.
22. PW-1 during his cross examination has admitted that Khasra no. 318 was acquired by LAC vide award no. 18/83-84.
He has further admitted that some of the part of Khasra no. 318 was handed over to DDA by the LAC.
However, he volunteered that built up portion was left out and not transferred to DDA.

He further admitted that he has not filed any document to show that at the time of acquisition of land of village Gharoli, the land measuring 296 bighas 17 biswas was left out from acquisition as the said area was found to be thickly populated and built up which was averred by him in his plaint.
The plaintiffs have heavily relied upon their family members names reflecting in Revenue records such as Khasra Khatauni to establish that they have been in ownership and possession of the suit land.
However, it is the settled position of law that reflection of parties name in revenue records cannot confer title.

This was also upheld in recent judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court titled as "Prabhagiya Van Adhikari Awadh Van Prabhag vs. Arun Civ Suit 6703/16 Surat Singh VS. DDA 11/19 Kumar Bhardwaj (dead) Thr. LRs(Civil Appeal no. 7017 of 2009, decided on 05.10.2021) wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held:
"26.

entities.text: Prabhagiya Van Adhikari Awadh Van Prabhag vs. Arun Civ Suit 6703/16 Surat Singh VS. DDA 11/19 Kumar Bhardwaj
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court in a judgment reported as Prahlad Pradhan and Ors V Sonu Kumhar and Ors. 7 negated argument of ownership based upon entries in the revenue records.

entities.text: Prahlad Pradhan and Ors V Sonu Kumhar and Ors. 7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held that the revenue record does not confer title to the property nor do they have any presumptive value on the title.

The court held 7(2019) 10 SCC 259 as under Surat Singh vs Dda on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185516918/
7 :
"5.

entities.text: Surat Singh vs Dda on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon

sentences.text: The contention raised by the appellants is that since Mangal Kumhar was the recorded tenant in the suit property as per the Survey Settlement of 1964, the suit property was his self-acquired property.
The said contention is legally misconceived since entries in the revenue records do not confer title to a property, nor do they have any presumptive value on the title.
They only enable the person in whose favour mutation is recorded, to pay the land revenue in respect of the land in question.

As a consequence, merely because Mangal Kumhar's name was recorded in the Survey Settlement of 1964 as a recorded tenant in the suit property, it would not make him the sole and exclusive owner of the suit property."
The six yearly Khatauni for the fasli year 1395 to 1400 to the effect that the land stands transferred according to the Forest Act as the reserved record is in respect of Khasra no. 1576.
It is only in the revenue record for the period 1394 fasli to 1395 fasli, name of the lessees find mention but without any basis.
The revenue record is not a document title.

Therefore, even if the name of the lesseee finds mention in the revenue record but such entry without any supporting documents of creation of lease contemplated under the Forest Act is inconsequential and does Civ Suit 6703/16 Surat Singh VS. DDA 12/19 not create any right, title or interest over 12 bighas of land claimed to be in possession of the lessee as a lessee of the Goan Sabha."

sentences.text: 23. In the present case, also similar to the decision in Prabhagiya Van Adhikari(supra) the manner in which the possession of plaintiffs/his predecessor in interest is shown in some Khasra Khatauni for period between 1977-78 i.e. the period before the notification of acquisition of Gharoli village by DDA i.e. Ex. PW-1/D1 raised doubts as to whether the plaintiffs were in continuous possession or not.
Furthermore, the name of the plaintiffs is not reflected in Ex. PW-1/3 i.e. Khasra Girdawari.
The plaintiffs have filed LSR spreadsheet Ex. PW-1/5 to show that the possession of Khasra no. 318 has not been taken by the Government.

However, this court is of the considered opinion that Ex.
PW-1/5 is not duly proved by the plaintiff as it is not signed.
The plaintiff has averred that some of the part of the Khasra no. 318 is acquired by DDA whereas some part was left behind being built up.
However, no such fact is reflected in Ex. PW-1/5.
No witness was examined by the plaintiff to prove the same.
Therefore, Ex. PW-1/5 cannot be relied upon by this court.
24. The plaintiffs have also filed Ex. PW-1/8 and Ex. PW-1/9 i.e. the copy of house tax receipt and copy of electricity receipt.
The plaintiffs have examined PW-4 and PW-5 to prove the aforesaid receipts.
PW-4 is the summoned witness from EDMC, House Tax Department who has deposed that there is no record of property bearing no. 56, Khasra no. 318 before 2013.

PW-5 is the summoned witness from BSES who also deposed that electricity connection in the suit property was energized on 21.11.2013.
25.

This court is of the considered opinion that the plaintiffs in Civ Suit 6703/16 Surat Singh VS.
DDA 13/19 order to show their possession qua the suit land applied for the house tax and electricity connection prior to filing of the suit.

sentences.text: However, the plaintiffs have considerably failed to show that they have been in continuous and settled possession before filing of the suit.

It is to note that the Surat Singh vs Dda on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185516918/

sentences.text: Even otherwise, the mere filing of electricity and house tax receipt of year 2013 cannot by itself confer ownership and title in respect of precious suit land.

26. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi took similar view in the judgment titled as "Nathuram Vs. DDA & Anr,"decided on 01.02.2022 RSA 64/2022 wherein the Hon'ble Court observed that mere sporadic or stray entries in the revenue record cannot confer title.
Mere mentioning in Khasra Girdawaris without any other concrete documents would not entitle the plaintiff to discharge the heavy onus that is placed on him.

27. The court observed that plaintiffs have a onus to establish that they had acquired the suit property through legally recognized documents such as registered Sale Deed, allottment from Government authorities.
28. In the present case, the plaintiffs have not produced any such document to show that they are owners of the suit property.
Furthermore, the plaintiff also failed to show that they are in continuous and settled possession of the suit land.

The plaintiff failed to show that the suit land is a built up land whereas the photographs which are marked as Mark XX by the defendant clearly show that the suit land is a vacant land, therefore, the plaintiffs herein can establish their possession in the suit land Civ Suit 6703/16 Surat Singh VS. DDA 14/19 only through documents.

entities.text: Civ Suit 6703/16 Surat Singh VS. DDA
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no such document is filed on behalf of the plaintiff which can establish their possession qua the suit property.

29. During the course of final arguments, Ld. Counsel for the plaintiff has argued that the acquisition proceedings qua the suit land are not complete as land is acquired under land acquisition only when the physical possession of the land is taken up under Section 16 of Land Acquisition Act.
30. This court does not find merits in the arguments of Ld.Counsel for the plaintiff as this fact was never pleaded in the plaint nor any evidence was led by the plaintiff.
Furthermore, the plaintiffs in their evidence have admitted that Khasra no. 318 was acquired by the LAC which was handed over to DDA and some part of Khasra no. 318 was also handed over to DDA.

Therefore, the plaintiffs cannot be allowed to blow hot and cold by submitting that Khasra no. 318 has been acquired by the DDA on one hand while on the other averring that the acquisition proceedings are not complete.
31. The plaintiffs have also examined PW-2 and PW-3.

Close scrutiny of their testimonies also show that they have not brought any document to show that plaintiff has a right, title or interest in the suit land which means they have also failed to prove the case of the plaintiff.
32. In view of the above, plaintiffs have considerably failed to prove that they have right, title or interest in the suit land or they are in settled possession of the suit land.

Issue no. 6
Whether the suit is bad for want of service of notice u/s 53B of DDA Act? OPD1 45.
As far as the issue no. 6 is concerned, it was encumbant upon the defendant no. 1 to substantiate that the suit is barred in view of the provisions u/s 53B of DDA Act.

Before proceeding Civ Suit 6703/16 Surat Singh VS. DDA 17/19 ahead with deciding the present issue, the court deems it fit to mention here that Section 53B is applicable to defendant no. 1 which provide issuance of mandatory notice.

sentences.text: Provisions of Section 53B of DDA Act and Section 80 of CPC are of similar nature.

Section 53B of DDA Act and Section 80 of CPC provide that to file a suit against DDA or against certain government agency as the case may be, it is mandatory upon the plaintiff to issue mandatory notice as the case may be and to wait for mandatory period of two months.

46. It is again pertinent to mention here that Section 53B of DDA Act provides certain exceptions where the mandatory notice can be waived in case of certain urgencies and the suit can be filed without issuance of mandatory notice.
47. In case of urgency or urgent reason, the plaintiffs have to seek leave of the court by specifically mentioning urgency.
48. In the present case in hand, the plaintiffs have not issued mandatory notice against defendant no. 1 i.e. notice under Section 53B of DDA Act.

The plaintiffs have filed an application u/s 80 (2)
CPC r/w Section 151 CPC for exemption from giving notice to Public Authority stating that the plaintiffs have apprehension that the suit land may be transferred, alienated.

49. Clause 3 of Section 53B of DDA Act provides that the serving of the mandatory notice upon DDA can be waived off if the only relief claimed is an injunction of which the object would be defeated by the giving of the notice or the postponement of the institution of the suit.

50. The present suit is filed not only for seeking the relief of injunction simplicitor but for also seeking the relief of declaration of ownership which clearly means that the exception provided in the aforesaid provision does not apply to the present Civ Suit 6703/16 Surat Singh VS. DDA 18/19 case.
51. Accordingly, issue no. 6 is decided in favour of the defendants and against the plaintiffs.
Relief 52.
In view of the above, the suit of the plaintiff is dismissed.

32. In view of the above, plaintiffs have considerably failed to prove that they have right, title or interest in the suit land or they are in settled possession of the suit land.
